content:
Key observations from the test image:
- Underside of a soybean leaf
- Gray/silvery coating across the leaf surface
- Small yellow-green spots visible
- Prominent veining
- Slightly fuzzy/downy texture on the leaf underside

This strongly suggests **Downy mildew** — the gray tufts on the lower leaf surface and light yellow-green spots are the hallmark symptoms. Let me confirm with the reference.

The reference confirms the match. The bottom-left panel of the Downy mildew reference shows the same gray-green underside coating with pale/yellow spots — identical to the test image. The grayish fungal growth (sporangiophores) on the lower leaf surface is the defining diagnostic feature for Downy mildew.

```json
{"prediction": "Downy_mildew", "confidence": 0.82, "reasoning": "The image shows the underside of a soybean leaf with a characteristic gray/silvery coating (tan-to-gray fungal tufts of sporangiophores) and scattered small yellow-green spots — the hallmark symptoms of Downy mildew. This matches both the symptom description ('tufts of tan to gray-colored fungal growth on the underside of infected leaves') and the reference collage which shows the same gray-green underside texture with pale lesions."}
```
